questions.question: What is the main purpose of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: It helps organizations manage AI risks and promote trustworthy, responsible AI development and use.
questions.supporting_passage: the goal of the AI RMF is to offer a resource ... to help manage the many risks of AI and promote trustworthy and responsible development and use

questions.question: What are the four core functions of the AI RMF?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage.
questions.supporting_passage: These functions - GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE - are broken down further into categories and subcategories.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Govern function?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Govern cultivates a culture of risk management and establishes policies, processes, responsibilities, and oversight across the AI lifecycle.
questions.supporting_passage: GOVERN is designed to be a cross-cutting function to inform and be infused throughout the other three functions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Map function?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Map establishes AI-system context and identifies intended use, stakeholders, impacts, and risks.
questions.supporting_passage: The MAP function establishes the context to frame risks related to an AI system.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Measure function?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Measure assesses, analyzes, benchmarks, and monitors AI risks and impacts using appropriate methods.
questions.supporting_passage: The MEASURE function employs quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-method tools, techniques, and methodologies.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Manage function?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Manage prioritizes risks and takes actions to respond to, mitigate, or manage them.
questions.supporting_passage: The MANAGE function entails allocating resources to the risks mapped and measured and regularly prioritizing them.

questions.question: Is the NIST AI RMF mandatory for every organization?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: No. It is voluntary.
questions.supporting_passage: The Framework is intended to be voluntary, rights-preserving, non-sector-specific, and use-case agnostic.

questions.question: Is the AI RMF designed for only one industry?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: No. It is non-sector-specific and adaptable across sectors and contexts.
questions.supporting_passage: The Framework is intended to be ... non-sector-specific, and use-case agnostic.

questions.question: When was AI RMF 1.0 published?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: January 2023.
questions.supporting_passage: January 2023

questions.question: Who is credited as the author of the AI RMF 1.0 publication?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Elham Tabassi.
questions.supporting_passage: Elham Tabassi

questions.question: What does the framework mean by trustworthy AI characteristics?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: They are characteristics used to describe and assess AI-system trustworthiness.
questions.supporting_passage: characteristics of trustworthy AI systems include valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient ...

questions.question: Name the trustworthy AI characteristics discussed in the framework.
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Valid and reliable; safe; secure and resilient; accountable and transparent; explainable and interpretable; privacy-enhanced; and fair with harmful bias managed.
questions.supporting_passage: valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy enhanced, and fair with harmful biases managed

questions.question: Does AI risk management apply only before deployment?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: No. It applies throughout the AI lifecycle, including development, deployment, operation, and monitoring.
questions.supporting_passage: Test, Evaluation, Verification, and Validation tasks are performed throughout the AI lifecycle.

questions.question: What types of methods can be used to measure AI risks?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods.
questions.supporting_passage: The MEASURE function employs quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-method tools, techniques, and methodologies.

questions.question: Why is testing important when assessing AI systems?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Testing, evaluation, verification, and validation assess system performance and trustworthiness throughout the lifecycle.
questions.supporting_passage: TEVV tasks ... examine the AI system or its components, or detect and remediate problems.

questions.question: Why should AI risk measurement methods, metrics, and results be documented?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Documentation supports transparency, accountability, communication, and review of risk assessments and decisions.
questions.supporting_passage: Documentation of measurement methods, results, and related decisions supports transparency and accountability.

questions.question: Is Govern relevant only at the beginning of the AI lifecycle?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: No. Govern is cross-cutting and informs the other functions throughout AI risk management.
questions.supporting_passage: GOVERN applies to all stages of organizations’ AI risk management processes and procedures.

questions.question: Why can involving different perspectives improve AI risk identification?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Diverse stakeholders can identify assumptions, impacts, risks, and affected groups that a narrow team may miss.
questions.supporting_passage: The GOVERN and MAP functions describe the importance of interdisciplinarity and demographically diverse teams.

questions.question: What actions can an organization take when an identified AI risk is unacceptable?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: It can prioritize and mitigate the risk, reassess or change the system or its use, or decide not to deploy or continue use.
questions.supporting_passage: MANAGE function activities include responding to, recovering from, and communicating about incidents and errors.

questions.question: How do Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage work together?
questions.label: answerable
questions.reference_answer: Govern provides cross-cutting oversight; Map establishes context; Measure assesses risks; Manage prioritizes and responds.
questions.supporting_passage: Functions organize AI risk management activities ... govern, map, measure, and manage AI risks.
